subject: Approval request: 5-year continuity guarantee + uplift ceiling for Horizon Health expansion
messages:
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>
To: Lorenzo Rossi <lorenzo@horizonhealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-22T09:14:00-08:00
Subject: Proposal + continuity package for Horizon expansion

Hi Lorenzo —

Thanks again for taking the call this morning. Per our conversation I've attached an updated proposal and draft SOW for the multi-region rollout you described. Key commercial highlights:

- 5-year committed run rate: $3,000,000 ARR (annual billing schedule)
- Initial year: 30% list discount on hosted API calls and dedicated capacity blocks
- Continuity guarantee: we will hold the contracted per-token rates for the full 5-year term, subject to agreed uplift ceilings (see below)
- Proposed uplift ceiling: +6% year-over-year on per-token rates, with an annual true-up tied to usage tiers rather than CPI

You asked about a narrow renewal protection clause: if Horizon moves to a materially different provider within the 5-year window due to performance issues unrelated to contracted SLAs, we will provide a partial pro-rate credit based on remaining committed seats — this is written into the attached draft but flagged for legal review.

Before we finalize for procurement, can you confirm Horizon is comfortable with the uplift ceiling mechanism tied to usage tiers (we can provide worked examples)? If yes, procurement asked for a signed commercial redline and DocuSign link.

Thanks — I’ve looped Marissa and Jordan to help with legal and pricing ops.

Best,
Tessa Morgan
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
T: 415-555-0167

Attachments: Horizon_HS_Proposal_v3.pdf (proposal summary), Draft_SOW_Horizon_2026.docx (scope), redwood_price_summary.csv (tiered uplift examples)

From: Lorenzo Rossi <lorenzo@horizonhealth.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-22T11:02:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Proposal + continuity package for Horizon expansion

Tessa —

Thanks, proposal looks reasonable at a glance. Two quick asks from procurement/legal before we circulate to execs: 1) Horizon requires a firm price-lock for the first 3 years (we can accept the uplift mechanism after that but want certainty early), and 2) we need an explicit uplift ceiling that caps any year-over-year increase at +4% if our usage stays within the specified tier. We understand aggressive commit discounts are tied to usage — our expectation is that the lock + lower cap are essential for our board.

Also, last time we saw broad language around "continuity credit" it was imprecise. Can we get explicit exit triggers and the calculation for any pro-rata credit? Procurement would like to see this in the contract.

If you can get a sign-off path from your side (legal & pricing) for 3-year firm lock + 4% Y/Y ceiling for years 1-3 and standard 6% thereafter, we can move to fast-track review.

Regards,
Lorenzo
VP, Cloud Platforms — Horizon Health

Subject: Fwd: Proposal + continuity package for Horizon expansion — pricing ops/legal review

Team —

Looping you in. Customer wants: firm 3-year price lock, 4% Y/Y cap for years 1-3, then revert to proposed 6% thereafter. They also want clarity on the continuity credit formula and exit triggers.

Commercial context: 5-year, $3M ARR commit; initial tooling and migration assistance included; concessions in question: deeper early-year cap (4%) and firm lock length (3 years vs our typical 2). Our standard guardrails allow exceptioning to 3 years at VP sales approval for strategic accounts, but the 4% cap in years 1-3 would be a below-policy pricing protection (we usually cap at 5% for comparable commits).

Requests:
- Legal: add explicit exit triggers and the pro-rata continuity credit calculation into SOW/contract (see doc attached).
- Pricing/Ops (Kimberly, Aditya): confirm delta impact to unit economics and whether 4% Y/Y for first 3 years materially changes the margin given the proposed discount and dedicated capacity commitments. Include an estimated worst-case uplift exposure table.

I recommend we put this to Executive approval given the deviation from standard cap. Tessa — can you summarize the commercial rationale (strategic importance, referenceability, likelihood to upsell) so I can attach to the approval request?

—Marissa

Attachments referenced: redwood_price_summary.csv (tiered uplift examples), Draft_SOW_Horizon_2026.docx

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>, Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-23T12:25:00-08:00
Subject: RE: Fwd: Proposal + continuity package for Horizon expansion — pricing ops/legal review

Marissa / team —

Quick summary from pricing ops:
- Baseline: proposed commercial yields ~42% gross margin at list discount 30% with dedicated pool amortization spread across committed tpu (tokens per unit) assumptions.
- Exposure: moving the Y/Y cap from 6% -> 4% for years 1-3 reduces expected revenue uplift under high inflation scenarios by ~1.8% cumulative vs our baseline model. Worst-case uplift exposure (if Horizon moves up usage tier each year) increases Redwood cost of goods by an additional ~$120k over 3 years.
- Recommendation: Approve the 3-year firm lock (we can operationalize in billing) but limit the 4% cap exception to a one-time concession subject to Executive approval and include an overage-sharing clause if usage growth >150% year-over-year.

I can attach a short spreadsheet with modeled scenarios for the approval note.

-Kimberly

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: CEO Execs Distribution <ceo_execs@redwood.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-24T15:02:00-08:00
Subject: Executive approval requested — Horizon Health: 3-year firm lock + temporary 4% uplift ceiling

Team —

TL;DR: Horizon Health (DL-2026-0894) is asking for a 5-year contract with a commercial construct that includes a firm 3-year price lock and a 4% year-over-year uplift ceiling for years 1–3 (then 6% thereafter). The account is strategic (national healthcare provider, potential reference, 3x pilot ARR expansion) and the committed ARR is $3M. We need Executive approval to grant the 4% Y/Y cap for the first 3 years (this is a deviation from policy where comparable deals are capped at 5–6%).

Why this matters:
- Strategic value: Horizon is a referenceable healthcare partner with heavy regulatory needs (SOC2 + private VPC roadmap). They are likely to expand into Dedicated and Private deployments over the next 18 months.
- Economic impact: Kimberly modeled the downside — estimated incremental cost exposure ~ $120k over 3 years in a high-growth usage scenario. Pricing still yields ~40%+ gross margin under base assumptions.
- Contract mechanics: Legal will surface an explicit continuity-credit formula and exit triggers in the SOW. Billing/Finance confirmed we can operationalize a 3-year firm lock and cap the uplift in the billing system.

Request to Execs: Approve one-time exception to permit 4% Y/Y uplift ceiling for years 1–3 (bound to deal DL-2026-0894), conditioned on:
1) Legal-approved exit triggers and pro-rata continuity credit language added to SOW;
2) An overage-sharing clause if usage growth exceeds 150% Y/Y;
3) Quarterly business reviews and a built-in 24-month check-in to revisit uplift ceilings as needed.

If approved, I will notify Tessa to send the redlined contract and DocuSign link.

Vote/Reply please (approve / deny / request changes).

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Head of Deal Desk, Redwood Inference
